transcript.text: The common causes are a lost power supply (socket, plug fuse or tripped breaker), a door that is not fully latching, or less commonly a control fault. First, check the wall switch is on and try another appliance in that socket; if it is a plug-in dishwasher, check the plug fuse only with it switched off and unplugged. Then close the door firmly and try again. When you press power, is the display or any light completely dead, or does it light up but not start?
completely dead, no lights at all. other sockets and lights work fine. the switch above the worktop is on and its neon is lit

A lit neon on the worktop switch shows the switch has a supply, but it does not prove power is reaching the dishwasher. The next useful check is the dishwasher’s own supply: if its plug and socket are accessible, switch the spur off, unplug the dishwasher, then plug a known-working lamp or charger into that socket and switch the spur back on. If that item does not work, it is a supply, socket, fuse or wiring issue; if it does work, the likely fault is inside the dishwasher, most often its mains input/control board, and that needs an engineer. If it is hard-wired or the socket cannot safely be reached, tell me that instead.
there's no plug I can get to, it goes through that switch above the worktop and I can't pull the dishwasher out. I've got no meter or spare fuse either. what now?

There is no further useful owner-safe check here without access to the connection or electrical test equipment. A lit neon only shows the spur has an incoming supply; it cannot confirm that power is leaving it and reaching the dishwasher. The two main possibilities are a failed fuse/connection in the spur or an internal mains-input/control-board fault in the dishwasher. Arrange an appliance engineer to prove the supply at the dishwasher first; if the spur has no output, that part is for an electrician. Avoid removing the spur faceplate or pulling the dishwasher out yourself.

Door not latching or door switch not being operated (medium)
